assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of time-reversal-invariant topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect, followed by the HgTe/CdTe observation, is a clean discovery that opened a new class of electronic phases. It is a clear case of theory prediction matched by decisive experiment on a well-defined material system, with broad influence on materials physics.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the Z2 classification and the quantum spin Hall proposal; Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental realization (with the Zhang-group HgTe prediction as a closely related contribution not on this credited list). Three names give a defensible theory-plus-experiment configuration, though other theorists (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang; Fu, Kane) have claims that cannot be represented here.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in multiple materials and by independent techniques, including transport and photoemission, for well over a decade. The interpretation is stable and recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: Credit for the 3D topological insulator and the HgTe prediction is split among people outside this candidate's credited names.
Overlap with the separate quantum anomalous Hall candidate may complicate how the discovery is bounded.
I rely on my own recollection of the history and have not verified the detailed priority claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum cascade laser is a genuine invention: a unipolar semiconductor laser whose wavelength is set by engineered layer thicknesses rather than the bandgap, realized in 1994 and now a workhorse of mid-infrared spectroscopy and sensing. It is the sort of discovery-or-invention the prize criteria describe, and its dependence on atomic-scale control of heterostructures and interfaces is something I appreciate from the materials side.
assessment.attribution: The Bell Labs team around Capasso, Faist and Cho is the natural core: Capasso for the concept and leadership, Faist for the first demonstration, Cho for the molecular-beam-epitaxy growth that made the structures possible. Sirtori, Sivco and Hutchinson were also co-authors and the original Kazarinov-Suris proposal predates the device, so allocation is not trivially clean.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of development, commercial devices and independent replication make confirmation and impact secure. Timing is arguably overdue.
uncertainties: The 1971 Kazarinov and Suris proposal complicates priority.
Whether growth technology (Cho) deserves a share alongside the two physicists is a judgement call.
Physics versus engineering classification may weigh against it for some members.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The magic-angle flat bands prediction and the observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the moire quantum materials field. The discovery is original, conceptually clear and has changed how layered materials are designed, with a strong tie to imaging and spectroscopy of local structure in van der Waals stacks.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the decisive 2011 prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the 2018 experimental discovery. The credited trio matches that theory-plus-experiment story well, although Cao as first author and other groups (Dean, Young, Yazdani, Kim) contributed to the broader field.
assessment.maturity: Roughly eight years old, widely reproduced, with active debate on the origin of superconductivity and correlated states. The core discovery is secure but the mechanistic interpretation is still evolving, so it is somewhat early.
uncertainties: Mechanism of superconductivity remains debated.
Sample-to-sample variation and twist-angle disorder raise reproducibility questions about details.
Possible early recognition compared with more settled topics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, with the magic-wavelength concept, is an invention that moved timekeeping to the 10^-18 level and enables tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy. Its originality and clarity are high, and a precise measurement platform is a natural prize subject.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice and led the first realizations; Ye's group pushed the performance and the strontium clock to record accuracy. Two names is a compact, fair configuration. Contributions from Hall, Hänsch and Wineland-type ion-clock work have been recognized elsewhere.
assessment.maturity: Independent clocks agree and are compared across laboratories; the technology is mature. Redefinition of the second is still pending, but that does not undercut the physics.
uncertainties: Prior prizes in frequency metrology might make some members see this as incremental.
Other contributors to the optical lattice clock concept are not on the list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-resolution angle-resolved photoemission turned a surface spectroscopy into a quantitative probe of band structure, gaps, kinks and quasiparticle dynamics in cuprates and other correlated materials. As an experimentalist in spectroscopy, I regard this as an instrument-and-method advance with lasting impact across quantum materials.
assessment.attribution: Shen and Campuzano are the two most clearly associated with the cuprate ARPES results; instrument development by many groups (including the synchrotron and laser sources and the detector advances) is spread more broadly, which complicates whether this is a discovery or a technique.
assessment.maturity: Decades of consistent results across laboratories and materials. The method is mature and timing is not premature, although the physics conclusions about the cuprates themselves remain unsettled.
uncertainties: The prize needs a specific discovery rather than a technique; the boundary is unclear.
Credit for instrumentation is dispersed across many groups.
Cuprate mechanism still lacks consensus.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond established a room-temperature solid-state spin system used in nanoscale magnetometry, biosensing and quantum information. The work is original and of broad use, including for local probing of materials.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko's 1997 single-spin detection and subsequent coherent control are the decisive experimental contributions. Lukin's group broadened it to quantum registers and sensing; a configuration with two or three names is plausible but the boundary of the discovery is fuzzy.
assessment.maturity: Well replicated worldwide, with growing applications. The sensing applications are still maturing, which makes timing reasonable but not urgent.
uncertainties: Allocation between the foundational detection work and the later sensing and register results is unresolved.
Some members may judge the field still in rapid development.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics created the architecture underlying most superconducting quantum processors and enabled strong coupling of artificial atoms to microwave photons. The conceptual and experimental advance is clear and influential.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf proposed and demonstrated the scheme in 2004; Girvin is credited and omitted here only because three laureates are the maximum. Choosing among four contributors is a genuine difficulty.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced widely and central to current devices, though recent recognition of superconducting-circuit macroscopic quantum effects may reduce the room for a further prize in this area soon.
uncertainties: Four credited names cannot all be recognized.
Overlap with recent prize recognition of superconducting circuits.
Engineering versus fundamental discovery distinction.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of iron-based high-temperature superconductivity in 2008 opened a second family of high-Tc materials and was a surprising result, reached through materials synthesis and characterization. It is a discovery in the sense the prize criteria use.
assessment.attribution: Hosono's group made the original discovery in LaFeAsO(F); Zhao and colleagues, and Chen's group, raised Tc above 50 K within weeks. The initial discovery is clearly Hosono's, so a shared prize requires judgement about the follow-up contributions.
assessment.maturity: Highly reproduced and extensively studied, but the pairing mechanism is still unresolved and the practical impact is limited relative to the cuprates.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism remains open.
Whether the Tc-raising results merit shared recognition is uncertain.
Practical consequences so far are modest.
